user_prompt: I need to push back on a late charge from my landlord. Draft something respectful that says I paid on time and they should drop the fee.
final_prompt:
I need to push back on a late charge from my landlord. Draft something respectful that says I paid on time and they should drop the fee.

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Hi Dana,

Thank you for the note regarding this month's rent. I've reviewed my lease, and I believe the $75 late fee was applied in error.

My payment was received on the 3rd, which falls within the grace period described in Section 4.2 of my lease. That section states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period, which runs through the 5th.

Could you please remove the $75 late fee from my account? I'd appreciate a brief confirmation once it has been corrected. I'm happy to send a copy of my payment confirmation if that would be helpful.

Thank you for your attention to this.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

runs.answer:
Your lease is on your side here. Section 4.2 says there's a grace period through the 5th and that no late fees may be charged during it. Dana's own email says rent was received on the 3rd, which falls inside that window. So the $75 fee appears to violate the lease.

Here's a reply you could send by email, which Section 9.4 allows:

---

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thanks for your message. I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee added to my account for this month.

Per Section 4.2 of my lease, rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and no late fees may be charged during the grace period. As your email notes, my rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period. The fee therefore isn't permitted under the lease.

Please remove the $75 late fee from my account and confirm in writing once that's done. I've attached [proof of payment, e.g., the portal confirmation or money order receipt] for your records.

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

A few tips:
- Attach proof of payment with the date visible (portal confirmation, bank statement, or money order receipt) so the 3rd is documented.
- Keep a copy of the email and your lease.
- If they refuse, you can escalate to the property management company or your local housing authority or tenant rights office, which can often help at no cost. Small claims court is also an option for fees charged in violation of a lease, though it's rarely needed for an amount this size.

Laws vary by location, so if your jurisdiction has specific late-fee rules, a local tenant rights group can confirm them.

Your lease is on your side here. Section 4.2 gives a grace period through the 5th and says no late fees may be charged during it. Dana's records show rent received on the 3rd, which falls inside that window, so the $75 fee shouldn't have been assessed.

You could send something like this by email, since Section 9.4 allows email notice:

---

Subject: Late fee dispute - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

I'm writing about the $75 late fee added to my account for this month. My records and your own show rent was received on the 3rd. Section 4.2 of my lease provides a grace period through the 5th and states that no late fees may be charged during that period. Since my payment was within the grace period, the fee doesn't apply under the lease.

Please remove the $75 charge from my account and confirm in writing. I'd appreciate a reply by [date].

Thank you,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

A few practical tips:

- **Keep proof of payment.** Save the date and method (portal confirmation, check image, money order receipt), in case they dispute when it was received.
- **Set a deadline.** A week or so is reasonable.
- **Don't pay the fee yet** if you can avoid it, or pay it under protest and note that in writing. Non-payment could otherwise muddy the record.
- **Escalate if needed.** If they refuse, check your local tenant rights organization or housing authority. Many jurisdictions also have rules on late fees beyond what the lease says, so those resources can tell you whether there are additional protections.
